The most expensive AI model is no longer the smartest business decision — and the C-suite is saying it out loud.

Satya Nadella, Nikesh Arora, and Brian Armstrong have all publicly stated that smaller, cheaper AI models can handle a significant share of enterprise workloads. Reuters reported this shift on June 29 as a defining trend in enterprise AI procurement.

Here is the number that should concern every CTO: 95% of enterprise AI usage still runs on frontier models. Yet routing techniques that combine cheap open-weight models for bulk tasks with frontier models only where needed can cut effective per-token costs by 70-90%. That is not a marginal optimization. That is a structural cost failure hiding in plain sight.

D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria put it bluntly: current growth rates for Anthropic and OpenAI are the fastest they will ever be. The implication is direct — as enterprises get smarter about model selection, the revenue concentration at the top of the market will compress. For AI providers, this means pricing pressure. For enterprises, it means the advantage goes to those who build cost-intelligent AI architectures now.

The direction is clear. AI budgets will not shrink — but the share going to frontier models will. The organizations that architect for this reality today will operate at fundamentally different unit economics than those that keep defaulting to the most expensive option.
